tweed_weaver.text: Tweed and Wool. Irish tweed is woven from sheep's wool, and it keeps the rain out, which is a full-time job around here.
Báinín is undyed wool, the colour of the sheep's own coat. The word comes from bán, which means white.
Behind the town, Mount Brandon rises nearly a thousand metres. The sheep up there have the best view in Kerry, and know it.
